newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria premier postpones Moscow gas trip.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria premier postpones Moscow gas trip.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim prime minister has postponed a visit to Moscow to sign a bilateral gas agreement at Russia's request, a government spokeswoman said on Thursday.

She said the Russian government would continue discussions on Monday before taking a decision on the draft intergovernmental agreement as some details in it were different from the initial Russian project.
"The pact needs the approval of the whole government, in the same way as it was approved today by the Bulgarian cabinet, which authorised premier Stefan Sofianski to sign it," she said.

Sofianski and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin were due to sign the agreement for Russian gas supplies to Bulgaria, transiting Russian gas to the Balkans and construction of new transiting pipelines on Friday in Moscow.
Sofianski is now expected to fly to Moscow on Tuesday or Wednesday, the spokeswoman told reporters.

On Tuesday Bulgarian and Russian officials, including senior officials from Russia's Gazprom GAZP.RTS, headed by vice-president Bogdan Bodzulyak, drafted the terms of the long-delayed agreement, which would turn Bulgaria into a centre for distributing Russian natural gas on the Balkans.
Under the draft agreement the new gas pipelines, which will be constructed on Bulgarian territory for transiting Russian gas to neighbouring countries, will be Bulgarian-owned.
The terms for building the new pipelines and the prices of gas supplies and transiting fees will be fixed in commercial contracts between Bulgargas and suppliers selected by Gazprom.
Bulgaria has more than 2,000 km of pipeline network, including 625 km of transit pipelines which receive and transmit gas from outside the country. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-9814245
